hints: Equal gradients and a shared point.

ladder.nudge: Equal gradients and a shared point.

manual.title: Domain of a root over a linear factor
manual.prompt: For $f(x)=\dfrac{\sqrt{x+3}}{x-1}$, state the natural domain, and find the value of $x$ for which $f(x)=0$.

manual.title: Equation with a two thirds power
manual.prompt: Solve $x^{2/3}=16$ for real $x$.
hints: Raise both sides to the power 3.

ladder.nudge: Raise both sides to the power 3.

manual.title: Break-even points for a curved revenue
manual.prompt: A business has cost $C=200+4x$ and revenue $R=12x-0.02x^{2}$ dollars for $x$ items. Find, to the nearest item, the break-even quantities.

diagram.alt: Graph drawn on x and y axes; 2 plotted lines, curves or sets of points are drawn; some of the plotted lines are dashed. Marked on the horizontal axis: 27, 373. Read the question for what it asks.

manual.title: Odd and even with trig factors
manual.prompt: Classify each as odd, even or neither: (a) $f(x)=x^{2}\cos x$ (b) $g(x)=x^{3}+\sin x$ (c) $h(x)=x+\cos x$.

manual.title: Algebraic fraction division that simplifies to one
manual.prompt: Simplify $\dfrac{x^{2}-9}{x^{2}+x-6}\div\dfrac{x-3}{x-2}$, stating any restrictions on $x$.

manual.title: Ticket sales with three prices
manual.prompt: A show sold $50$ tickets: adults at $\$20$, children at $\$8$ and seniors at $\$12$, taking $\$680$ in total. Twice as many children's tickets as seniors' tickets were sold. How many of each were sold?

manual.title: Quadratic that is always positive
manual.prompt: Find the values of $k$ for which $kx^{2}-4x+k>0$ for all real $x$.

manual.title: Acute angle between two lines through the origin
manual.prompt: Find the acute angle between the lines $y=x$ and $y=\sqrt3x$ using their angles of inclination.

manual.title: Tangent to a circle at a 3-4-5 point
manual.prompt: Show that the tangent to $x^{2}+y^{2}=25$ at $(3,4)$ has equation $3x+4y=25$.

diagram.alt: Graph drawn on x and y axes; 3 plotted lines, curves or sets of points are drawn; some of the plotted lines are dashed. Read the question for what it asks.

manual.title: Unknown coefficient for perpendicular lines
manual.prompt: Find $k$ if the lines $kx+2y=5$ and $3x-y=1$ are perpendicular.
